access_links.label: RIPE Labs: Superstorm Sandy and the global internet

dedupe_keys.name: measurements of internet outages during hurricane sandy 2012

description: This post-event and recovery case brings together network measurement studies of how Hurricane Sandy affected the internet in the north-eastern United States at the end of October 2012. Researchers at the University of Southern California's Information Sciences Institute probed a sample of address blocks across the internet with pings and treated blocks that stopped responding as outages; they found that the outage rate in US networks roughly doubled when the storm made landfall and took about four days to return to normal, and confirmed that the rise came from New York and New Jersey. Renesys looked at BGP routing and saw traffic shift away from New York, a major international hub, as carriers sought other paths, while a RIPE Labs and ISP Column analysis by Geoff Huston counted some 3,721 routes withdrawn and not restored during 14 hours around landfall at one observation point. Flooding and power loss at Manhattan buildings such as 75 Broad Street and 111 Eighth Avenue, which house data centres and interconnection points, lie behind many of these outages. Coverage: the United States with a focus on New York and New Jersey, late October to early November 2012. Format and access: technical report PDF and blog analyses, free. Caveats: the ISI sample is small and mostly random, and ping-based detection misses networks that block probes. Simulation uses: recovery curves of edge networks after coastal storms, hazard exposure of interconnection hubs and cascading effects of power loss on connectivity. Related records: the Sandy data-centre case covers the same buildings from inside, IODA provides outage detection data, and the Lights Out study projects future coastal exposure.
